subject: biochemistry
title: Carbohydrate and lipid chemistry: isomerism, glycosidic bonds and lipid classifications

steps.tx: Monosaccharides exhibit structural and stereochemical **isomerism** that dictates biological recognition. D- and L-isomers are designated by the asymmetric carbon farthest from the carbonyl group. Epimers differ in configuration around a single chiral carbon; D-glucose and D-galactose are C-4 epimers, whereas D-glucose and D-mannose are C-2 epimers. In solution, open-chain aldoses cyclize into alpha- and beta-anomers via hemiacetal formation.
steps.say: Monosaccharides display stereoisomerism critical for enzyme recognition. D- and L-designations reflect the chiral carbon furthest from the carbonyl. Epimers differ at a single carbon: glucose and galactose are C-4 epimers, while glucose and mannose are C-2 epimers. Ring closure produces alpha and beta anomers.

steps.tx: Disaccharides and polysaccharides are formed through **glycosidic** bonds joining an anomeric hydroxyl to another alcohol. Maltose possesses an alpha-1,4 linkage, whereas lactose has a beta-1,4 linkage hydrolyzed by intestinal brush border lactase. Sucrose links glucose and fructose via an alpha-1,beta-2 bond, locking both anomeric carbons and eliminating reducing sugar properties. Glycogen contains alpha-1,4 chains with alpha-1,6 branches.
steps.say: Glycosidic bonds join an anomeric carbon to another sugar alcohol. Maltose has an alpha-1,4 bond, while lactose features a beta-1,4 bond broken by lactase. Sucrose connects both anomeric carbons in an alpha-1, beta-2 linkage, making it non-reducing. Glycogen has alpha-1,4 backbones and alpha-1,6 branches.

steps.tx: The image lines up three ball and stick disaccharides with glowing links. Maltose joins glucose units through an **alpha linkage** while lactose uses a **beta linkage** at the marked **anomeric carbon**. Sucrose locks both anomeric carbons together, which explains why it cannot reduce copper tests whereas maltose and lactose can.
steps.say: The models show maltose with an alpha link, lactose with a beta link, and sucrose joining both anomeric carbons. Each anomeric carbon is labeled. Locking both ends in sucrose removes the free end that gives a positive result with copper reagents. Use the link type to predict digestion and test results.

steps.tx: Fatty acids are amphipathic carboxylic acids classified by **saturation** and hydrocarbon chain length. Saturated fatty acids like palmitate and stearate pack densely into rigid membranes. Unsaturated fatty acids contain cis-double bonds that introduce rigid kinks, increasing membrane fluidity and lowering melting points. Essential fatty acids, linoleic acid and alpha-linolenic acid, cannot be synthesized because human desaturases cannot introduce double bonds beyond carbon nine.
steps.say: Fatty acids are classified by chain length and saturation. Saturated fatty acids pack tightly to increase rigidity. Cis-unsaturated double bonds introduce kinks that boost membrane fluidity. Linoleic and alpha-linolenic acids are essential because humans cannot desaturate beyond carbon nine.

steps.tx: The image splits a membrane into tightly packed straight chains and loose bent chains. Straight **saturated fatty acids** like palmitate stack closely and lower **membrane fluidity**. Bent **cis double bonds** in oleate create kinks that push lipids apart and raise fluidity. Link chain shape to melting behavior in exam questions.
steps.say: The left side shows straight saturated chains packed tight with low fluidity. The right side shows cis unsaturated chains with a clear kink and wide spacing with high fluidity. The kink stops tight packing. More cis bonds means a more fluid membrane at body temperature.

steps.tx: Triacylglycerols function as the primary **reservoir** of metabolic energy in mammals. Three fatty acid molecules are esterified to a glycerol backbone, forming completely uncharged neutral lipids. Stored anhydrously within white adipocyte lipid droplets, triacylglycerols yield thirty-seven kilojoules per gram upon complete combustion, over twice the caloric density of glycogen, while requiring zero hydration weight for storage.
steps.say: Triacylglycerols serve as the body's chief fuel reservoir. Three fatty acids esterify to glycerol, forming neutral uncharged lipids. Stored anhydrously in adipocytes, they yield thirty-seven kilojoules per gram on oxidation, more than twice the energy density of hydrated glycogen.
